topics.description: Passwords are stored as one-way hashes, with a per-user salt so identical passwords do not produce identical hashes.

topics.description: Symmetric uses one shared key and is fast; asymmetric uses a key pair and solves key distribution. TLS uses asymmetric to agree a symmetric key.
topics.notes: A named comparison; the reason both exist together in TLS is the insight. Depth rationale: either end of a named confusable pair, which is exactly the shape a multiple-choice comparison question takes.
